subject: Reasoning
topic: Cause and Effect — Statement Relationships (Set W7)

questions.stem:
In each question, two statements are given. Choose the relationship:
A) Statement I is the cause; Statement II is its effect
B) Statement II is the cause; Statement I is its effect
C) Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause
D) Both I and II are independent causes/effects with no direct relationship

Statement I: The school announced early dismissal for students today.
Statement II: A severe cyclone warning was issued for the coastal region.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: B is correct. The cyclone warning (II) is the cause — it prompted authorities to dismiss students early for safety (I). A cyclone warning causing schools to close is a clear, logical cause-effect chain.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The price of petrol increased by Rs 5 per litre last week.
Statement II: Many daily commuters switched to public transport or carpooling.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: A is correct. The petrol price hike (I) is the cause. In response, commuters shifted to cheaper alternatives (II). Rising fuel costs directly motivate people to seek more economical transport options.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The city's wholesale markets are reporting record high vegetable prices this week.
Statement II: Demand for packaged and processed foods has risen significantly in the city.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both statements are effects of a common underlying cause — a disruption in vegetable supply (such as unseasonal rains or transport strike). The shortage drives up vegetable prices (I) AND pushes consumers toward packaged alternatives (II). Neither statement directly causes the other.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The municipal corporation announced a water holiday for the eastern zone tomorrow.
Statement II: Several main water supply pipelines were damaged during road construction work.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: B is correct. Pipeline damage during road work (II) is the cause. The damage disrupts water supply, forcing the corporation to declare a water holiday (I) while repairs are made. This is a clear infrastructure cause-effect chain.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The government reduced import duty on electronic goods.
Statement II: Prices of imported smartphones fell in the domestic market.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: A is correct. Reducing import duty (I) directly lowers the cost of importing goods, which passes through to lower retail prices (II). This is a straightforward economic cause-effect relationship in trade policy.

questions.stem:
Statement I: Long queues were seen at government ration shops across the district.
Statement II: Several private grocery stores ran out of essential food commodities.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both statements are effects of a common cause — likely a disruption in food supply chains (a strike, flooding, or panic-buying announcement). The shortage caused queues at ration shops (I) AND stock depletion in private stores (II). Neither event directly caused the other.

questions.stem:
Statement I: Several students in the school topped the district in the board examinations.
Statement II: The school's principal was awarded the Best School Administrator prize at the state level.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: A is correct. Outstanding academic results by students (I) is the likely cause that led to the principal being recognised and awarded (II). Academic excellence at a school typically reflects well on its leadership, making I the cause and II the resulting honour.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The city experienced massive traffic congestion on all major roads yesterday.
Statement II: The heavy rainfall last night flooded several low-lying streets.
Statement III (context only, not an option): A major festival procession was also planned for the same day.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: B is correct. Flooding of streets (II) restricted traffic to fewer roads, causing congestion (I). The context hint of a festival procession adds to the scenario but the primary cause stated in the statements is the flooding. Flooding → reduced road capacity → traffic jam.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The state government launched a free skill-training programme for unemployed youth.
Statement II: Unemployment rates among 18-25 year olds in the state had reached a decade-high.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: B is correct. The alarming unemployment figures (II) prompted the government to launch the skill-training intervention (I). This is a policy response pattern: a social problem (unemployment at decade-high) causes a government action (skill programme). II is the cause, I is the response/effect.

questions.stem:
Statement I: The city's air quality index dropped to 'Severe' category for 10 consecutive days.
Statement II: Schools and colleges in the city were ordered to switch to online classes.

options.option_text: I is the cause; II is the effect
II is the cause; I is the effect
Both are effects of a common cause
Both are independent causes with no direct relationship

questions.explanation: A is correct. Severe air pollution (I) is the cause. To protect students from toxic air, authorities ordered online classes (II). This is a public health response: hazardous environment → precautionary school closure/online shift. I causes II.
